aciklama:
Everyone fears the elevator plunging - but the physics make it almost impossible. Here is why.

#shorts #engineering #science #howitworks #safety

sahneler.metin: Everyone fears the cable snapping and the car dropping.
But even if every cable snapped at once, it would not fall.
Each car hangs from several steel cables, not one.
Any single cable can hold the entire car by itself.
If they all failed, an overspeed brake grips the rails.
Springs at the bottom would cushion whatever was left.
Physics is quietly protecting you on every floor.

vaka.mekanizma: redundant ropes and an overspeed safety brake
vaka.ders: redundancy makes free fall almost impossible
vaka.yanilgi: The elevator safety brake isn't new — Elisha Otis demonstrated it in 1854 by having the rope cut while he stood on the platform.
vaka.tartisma: Knowing all this, which is riskier: the elevator or the stairs?
